questions.question_text: Which one among the following is an early sign of opioid withdrawal?
questions.explanation:
Early signs and symptoms of opioid withdrawal starts within 6-12 hours for short-acting drugs, and 24- 36 hours for longer-acting drugs.
Symptoms include muscle aches, anxiety and agitation, sleep issues, running nose and yawning. Nausea and vomiting, diarrhoea, goose
bumps, stomach cramps, depression or dysphoria and intense drug cravings start later (late onset symptoms)

The prevalence of a condition is 10%. A new diagnostic test ('test A') has a sensitivity of 95% and false positive rate of 5%. What is the post
test probability?
questions.explanation:
According to Bayes' Theorem, if you know the pretest probability and likelihood ratio of a test, you can �nd the post test probability. There
are two ways of computing post-test probability. If you have Bayesian nomogram, you can simply connect the dots indicating pretest
probability and LR value, to get the third point indicating post-test probability. If you don't have a nomogram at hand, you have to then use
the following formula: post-test odds = pretest odds x LR (Note that this formula uses odds, not probability rates). In this question,
prevalence = pretest probability = 10/100. So pre test odds = 10/90 (as odds = probability / [1-probability]) LR+ = true positivity rate/ false

sleeping well and unable to enjoy things. She is fatigued, irritable and washes her baby's feeding bottle several times each day, worried that
it is contaminated. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

The primary diagnosis is Postnatal depression. This presentation is most likely to represent an episode of post-natal depression as the

questions.explanation:
Hypokalaemia is potentially life-threatening due to the risk of cardiac arrhythmias. A low haemoglobin, albumin and urea are relatively

Mr Walsh is a 45-year-old man who is about to undergo ECT. He is on a medication, which requires the dose of ECT to be reduced. Which of
the following drugs is he likely to be taking?
questions.explanation:
Lithium is associated with an increased risk of delirium, prolonged seizures, toxic lithium levels, and prolonged neuromuscular blockade. A
combination of ECT and lithium is not absolutely contraindicated but the increased risks must be borne in mind when considering the
relative advantages and disadvantages. This would generally restrict concurrent use to emergencies. Lithium can be held the day before,
maintained at the lowest therapeutic dose or changed to an alternative medication.

after he recovers should he continue to take an antipsychotic medication?
questions.explanation:
There is reasonable evidence that continuing antipsychotic medication for 6 months after the resolution of an episode of mania reduces
relapse rates compared to stopping it abruptly. However, there is no strong evidence for continuing for longer than 6 months.

health conditions is he most likely to be experiencing?
questions.explanation:
Patients with hypochondriasis have a high rate of psychiatric comorbidity. In one outpatient clinical series, 88% of patients with

SSRIs are generally used in anorexia nervosa if pharmacological treatment is being considered. Venlafaxine has also been studied in clinical
trials. While concerns have been raised about QTc prolongation with high dose Citalopram this can be managed via monitoring ECGs.
Citalopram has one of the better evidence bases for medications in anorexia nervosa. Mirtazapine can markedly increase appetite, which
may be distressing for patients recovering from anorexia nervosa.

Clozapine should be avoided in breastfeeding mothers as it is transferred into the breast milk and there have been recorded cases of

questions.question_text: 'Sequential Diagrammatic reformulation' (SDR) is seen in what type of therapy?
questions.explanation:

map of problematic patterns and reciprocal roles. The procedures are depicted and interlinked in �ow-chart format. The aim of such
diagrams is to amplify understanding of often-complex procedural sequences and their inter-relationships in a way that words alone cannot.
SDR's are often elaborated by around the sixth or seventh session. (Ref: Denman, C., 2001. Cognitive–analytic therapy. Advances in
Psychiatric treatment, 7(4), pp.243-252.)

mechanism used in this situation is called
questions.explanation:

defence mechanism employed in this situation is called Manic defence. The potential sadness and anguish about the mother's death is
defended against by 'acting out the opposite': a sense of elation.

little information available about his past history. Investigations, including blood tests, are performed to try and determine a cause for his
presentation. Which of the following blood results are most likely to be responsible?
questions.explanation:
The diagnosis is Delirium. Hyponatraemia is more likely to cause delirium than the other abnormalities listed. Hypokalaemia is more likely to
cause fatigue, constipation and muscular abnormalities, including cardiac muscle. A urea of that level could be normal for this patient in
view of the usual deterioration in renal function with age. A mild anaemia would not usually cause delirium, nor would a small reduction in
albumin.

considering treating him with ECT. Which of the following conditions is an indication for ECT?
questions.explanation:
Catatonia, associated with self-neglect and poor or absent oral intake, can be life-threatening, and ECT is indicated in such instances to
preserve life.

questions.question_text:
Mrs Robinson is a 72-year-old lady with moderate dementia whom you have just seen in the diagnostic memory clinic. She has
hypertension, hyperlipidemia and is a current smoker. Her CT scan showed multiple old infarcts and severe small vessel disease. There was
no evidence of hippocampal atrophy. Which of the following interventions is NOT speci�c for Mrs Robinson?

options.text: Screening and treatment of diabetes if present

questions.explanation:
Patients with cognitive impairment and clinical or radiologic evidence of cerebrovascular pathology should be screened and treated for
vascular risk factors. There are limited trials comparing the treatment of vascular risk factors and impact on vascular dementia, however
current advice is to try to reduce vascular risk especially as part of secondary stroke prevention. Therefore, smoking cessation, screening for
diabetes and statins are indicated. Donepezil is not indicated unless there is an Alzheimer's component to the dementia (NICE Guideline 97).
Group Cognitive Stimulation Therapy should be o�ered to those with mild to moderate dementia (NICE Guideline 97). (References: Wright et
al, 2017. Treatment and prevention of vascular dementia. dementia, Dementia: assessment, management and support for people living with dementia and their carers. NICE guideline [NG97]
Published date: June 2018, independence-and-wellbeing)

older age; it usually presents around the age of 40-50. While Huntington's can show anticipation, with o�spring showing earlier onset of
symptoms, such a marked gap would be highly unusual.

questions.question_text:
Risk assessment is a core element of psychiatric practice. Risks can include those to the self, to others, vulnerability and ability to safely live
in the community. Which of the following is true regarding risk assessment?

options.text: Historical factors are considered more important than clinical factors
Demographic factors are thought to be more important than historical factors
Recent and older historical incidents are equally relevant
Structured professional judgement is more relevant than clinical judgement

correct_answer.text: Structured professional judgement is more relevant than clinical judgement

questions.explanation:
A structured professional judgement, utilising clinical expertise and a relevant risk assessment tool, is generally considered to be more
robust than a pure clinical assessment. Clinical factors are important in terms of putting historical factors into contexts, for example, a
signi�cant history of violence in a well patient may not indicate acutely increased risk, whereas an aggressive patient without a relevant
history would be considered to pose a higher risk. More recent risk incidents are felt to be more important to the assessment than older
ones.

prison after serving a sentence for actual bodily harm. He was reviewed by a psychologist prior to release to determine his risk to others in
the future. Which of the following is most accurate regarding short to medium term risk assessment?

options.text: Dynamic risk factors are most important to consider
Risk factors for violent and sexual o�ending are the same
Substance misuse history is unlikely to modify risk
Static risk factors are most important to consider
The relevant risk factors for male and female o�enders are the same

correct_answer.text: Dynamic risk factors are most important to consider

questions.explanation:
Dynamic risk factors, such as substance misuse, engagement with relevant interventions and expression of anger, are thought to be more
relevant for risk assessment in the short term. Static risks, such as childhood experiences, previous violent incidents and demographic
factors, are thought to be more relevant over the longer term.

questions.explanation:
Suicide is the leading cause of maternal death and in women with post-partum psychosis 2/1000 have been found to commit suicide usually
by violent means. Infanticide is reported to occur in around 4% of cases of post-partum psychosis. Neglect can occur in the context of
confusion and disorganization. At present the primary concern is Jane's delusions about her baby which place the baby at very high risk.
Delusions such as those described above are extremely high risk and will dictate the immediate management, which would likely be
admission to a hospital and initiation of antipsychotic treatment. Absconding and further deterioration are of course a concern, but are not
the primary concern at this point. (Reference: Payne J. Postpartum psychosis: Epidemiology, pathogenesis, clinical manifestations, course,
assessment, and diagnosis. UpToDate. 2018. Available: pathogenesis-clinical-manifestations-course-assessment-and-diagnosis)
